approved_findings: The November same-URL capture keeps the test-key embedded onramp purpose, domain allowlist, server-created OnrampSession/client-secret handoff, React loadStripeOnramp and mounted iframe, callbacks, and sandbox context (old 4-96, 98-233; new 5-9, 171-305, 848-902). The new 940-line capture also flattens many language/framework code panels and setup commands into one text stream (new 11-170, 306-845); these adjacent snippets are alternatives, not one runnable program or a demonstrated successful purchase.

The new capture adds server examples in Ruby, Python, PHP, Go, .NET and Java alongside Node and a separate direct browser-script path (new 37-170, 306-338, 702-845, 866-900). The old capture is specifically Node/React (old 8-96). The existing source summary line 13 remains accurate for its May raw but should be dated and expanded to acknowledge the November variants without blending incompatible examples.

For the direct script path, the November guide explicitly says load Stripe.js and crypto-js scripts from Stripe domains rather than bundling or self-hosting (new 866-872). The existing source only describes the React package path (source 27-39); keep the browser-script qualification scoped to the script variant, not an invented ban on installing the React packages.

Both captures retain limited-beta and custom-extension prose (old 18-22; new 848-852). However the new Java sample invokes client.v1().crypto().onrampSessions().create(params) and a .NET OnrampSessionService (new 139-170), which conflicts with an unqualified assertion that no official library has built-in endpoint support. The source line 17 and concept's Embedded Integration section should preserve the older Node custom-extension example as dated, narrow the broad library claim, and record the new-page internal tension rather than infer general availability.

Existing source line 25 and concept's Embedded Integration section call destination_currency, destination_exchange_amount, destination_network and customer_ip_address 'required'. Both captures show these fields passed in a server example (old 43-57; new 24-36), but neither supplies a complete request schema proving universal requiredness. Reword as the sample's sent fields. The browser submits transaction_details; the server obtains the IP separately, so the wording must preserve client/server identity.

The source's callbacks and sample transaction values remain example-specific (old 117-146, 227-229, 287-289; new 178-209, 299-304). Session status updates are not evidence of payment finality or delivered crypto. The page states the session object is intended to avoid charging a customer twice (new 848-850) but shows no executed transaction, webhook receipt, settlement, or bank result.

Preserve limited-beta wording as captured, qualified to the page/date and reconciled with newer variant snippets before broad SDK claims (old 22; new 852, 139-170).

Preserve the domain allowlist and test-key/sandbox framing, and do not infer live eligibility or completed crypto delivery (old 4-6, 96; new 9, 896-902).

No onramp session was created or paid in this review; the document's lifecycle description cannot prove a charge, final crypto delivery, or a bank receipt.
